acceptance: `derived_block` no longer says nothing in the pull request can change what the check attests, and a unit test pins the replacement text.
The Derived paths section of `docs/consumer-policy.md` states the same limit, or this item records that its current wording (lines 174 and 192) already does.
The change is in a Theseus release that BenchBox has promoted, shown by a recorded run id whose brief carries the new text.
description:
#### Problem
`derived_block` in `src/theseus_reviewer/render.py` (starts at line 406 on origin/main `409f610`; the text is at line 411) tells the reviewer that the derivation "is attested by the project check `<name>`, which Theseus does not run or verify; nothing in this pull request can change what that check attests".
- **Theseus cannot know that.** On BenchBox the pull request's own `manifest.json` chooses which source runs the check rebuilds from.
- **The hosted reviewer called it false.** In D8 on BenchBox #4541 (finding 4711372814 at `50404b86d3`) it said: "Here that claim is false, because the manifest is pull request content."
- **It conflicts with ADR 0001.** A statement about what a consumer's check verifies breaks the separation of concerns: Theseus states only what it can see.

#### Change
Reword `derived_block` so it says only these things:
- the check is named by the consumer's policy, read from the trusted base;
- Theseus does not run it or verify it, and does not know what it accepts;
- the summary is untrusted pull request data.

Keep the instruction not to read the data files. Update the brief tests.

#### Decision gates
- Ship it in the next Theseus release, or as a release of its own if the owner asks.
- Show the owner any change to what the reviewer is told to block on before it is committed.

#### Guardrails
- Name no consumer in the text.
- Make no change to eligibility rules or to the not-read instruction.
- Follow the release procedure. BenchBox adopts the change by lock promotion.

#### Verification rubric
- **Pass:** the rendered brief contains no claim about what the attesting check covers, and a unit test pins the new text. The released text is read from the brief in one BenchBox summary-only verdict run's log or artifact, with the run id recorded.
- **Fail:** any wording that asserts properties of the consumer's check.
